claims.claim: The fixed-k problems are monotone under padding: k-Induced Disjoint Paths reduces to ℓ-Induced Disjoint Paths for every fixed ℓ≥k while preserving H3-freeness. Moreover, k=1 is linear-time solvable and every fixed-k problem is in NP.
claims.evidence: Disjointly adjoining ℓ−k terminal K2 components gives an exact many-one reduction: each added pair has only its isolated edge as a route, and restriction recovers precisely the original linkage. Since H3 is connected and has eight vertices, the union is H3-free exactly when the original promised instance is. For k=1, connectivity is necessary and sufficient; a BFS/DFS establishes connectivity, and a shortest terminal path is induced. A collection of fixed-k simple path sequences has polynomial length and all linkage conditions are polynomially checkable.
claims.witness: For an input G, the forward witness is any original linkage together with the ℓ−k isolated designated edges; the reverse witness is obtained by deleting those forced edges. For k=1, a shortest s-t path is the certificate.
claims.search_method: Direct reconstruction of both directions of the padding reduction, followed by certificate-size and shortest-path checks under the source model.

claims.claim: Every H3-free graph is 6-degenerate, with the constant sharp; additionally, two vertices of degree at least three can never be at distance exactly three. Thus an n-vertex H3-free graph has at most 6n−21 edges for n≥7, and every connected H3-free graph of minimum degree at least three has diameter at most two.
claims.evidence: For a shortest u-x-y-v path, degree at least three supplies two additional neighbors at each endpoint. Shortestness excludes connector vertices and makes the two leaf pairs disjoint, yielding the eight distinct vertices and seven required edges of H3. Separately, every minimum-degree-seven graph contains every eight-vertex tree by parent-first greedy embedding, so every subgraph of an H3-free graph has a vertex of degree at most six. The degeneracy edge sum is 6(n−7)+21=6n−21. K7 is H3-free by order and has degeneracy six. A geodesic of length at least three in a connected minimum-degree-three graph would contradict the distance-three result using its first and fourth vertices.
claims.witness: K7 certifies sharpness of the degeneracy constant and attains 6·7−21=21 edges. The distance-three witness construction uses connector u-x-y-v and two distinct unused neighbors at each endpoint.
claims.search_method: Direct extremal and embedding proof, with all distinctness conditions in the H3 construction checked explicitly.

claims.claim: The induced-path fan threshold is seven edges: if an induced path in an H3-free graph has at least seven edges and every internal vertex has degree at least three, then every internal vertex has degree exactly three and all internal vertices have the same unique neighbor outside the path. Consequently, every run of at least six consecutive internal degree-at-least-three vertices on an arbitrary induced path is a fan about one off-path vertex.
claims.evidence: For P=p0…p7, each O_i=N(p_i)\V(P), 1≤i≤6, is nonempty. If a∈O_i and b∈O_{i+3} are distinct, p_i-p_{i+1}-p_{i+2}-p_{i+3}, with leaves p_{i−1},a,p_{i+4},b, is an H3 subgraph. Hence O_i=O_{i+3} is a singleton. Writing the three singleton values as a,b,c, the connectors p1-a-p4-p5 and p2-b-p5-p6 produce H3 whenever a≠b or b≠c, respectively. Thus all six sets equal one singleton; inducedness leaves each internal vertex exactly its two path neighbors and that hub. Overlapping seven-edge windows share internal vertices whose unique third neighbor identifies their hubs, proving the longer-path and run statements.
claims.witness: The forced H3 embeddings are (centers p_i,p_{i+3}; connector internals p_{i+1},p_{i+2}) for unequal distance-three off-neighbors, then centers p1,p5 and p2,p6 for unequal residue-class hubs.
claims.search_method: Universal set-and-distinctness proof, supplemented by exact enumeration of every nonempty off-neighbor assignment over two and three named outside vertices; all 118,378 assignments were checked with no counterexample.

claims.claim: The seven-edge threshold, and equivalently the six-vertex run threshold, is best possible.
claims.evidence: In the stated nine-vertex graph, p0…p6 is induced and p1,…,p5 all have degree three, while their common off-path neighborhood is empty: p3 uses q and the other four use h. Exact edge-preserving enumeration over all 9P8=362880 injections of labeled H3 found zero embeddings. The independent connector test found 20 simple three-edge candidate connectors up to reversal and no feasible choice of four distinct leaves. Therefore a six-edge path, equivalently a run of five branching vertices, need not have the fan conclusion.
claims.witness: Vertices p0,…,p6,h,q; path edges p_i p_{i+1}; additional edges hp1,hp2,hp4,hp5,qp3.
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of labeled H3 subgraph injections and independent connector-plus-leaf feasibility enumeration.

claims.claim: H3-free graphs admit an arbitrary-routing-plus-matching normal form. Let R be any graph and M a matching on V(R), disjoint from E(R). Replace every edge of R by a four-edge path and retain every edge of M unsubdivided, obtaining G(R,M). Then G(R,M) is H3-free. With all terminals in V(R), induced linkages in G(R,M) correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M such that every M-edge whose two endpoints are selected is itself used between consecutive vertices of one path. In particular, the H3-free class has unbounded treewidth.
claims.evidence: Every possible H3 center must be an original vertex because subdivision vertices have degree two. A three-edge simple path starting through an R-corridor ends at a subdivision vertex; one starting through M reaches an original after one edge but, because M is a matching, its remaining two edges must enter a corridor and again end at a subdivision vertex. Thus two possible centers cannot be joined by the required three-edge connector. Any path with original endpoints traverses each entered corridor completely, so contraction and lifting are inverse. Subdivided unused R-edges create no adjacency among selected vertices; precisely the unsubdivided M-edges can create chords or cross-path edges, and the stated consecutive-use rule is exactly what excludes them. For M empty and R=K_m, contracting corridors gives a K_m minor, hence unbounded treewidth.
claims.witness: The family G(K_m,∅) is H3-free and contains K_m as a minor. Corridor contraction/lifting supplies the explicit bijection for arbitrary R and M.
claims.search_method: Direct degree and path-length analysis plus contraction/lifting proof; exact finite stress test covered 328 normal-form hosts, 3,011 base paths, and 312 disjoint base-path pairs through |V(R)|=4.

claims.claim: In the routing-plus-matching normal form, matching edges cannot be treated as forbidden pairs even when the routing graph is just two disjoint paths: there is an H3-free two-pair instance whose straight rail routes violate the matching conflicts but whose paths switch rails through four matching edges and form an induced linkage.
claims.evidence: The two displayed switched base paths are vertex-disjoint and together select all twelve rail vertices. Each of the four matching edges is used consecutively on its appropriate switched path. Every unused rail edge is subdivided and therefore creates no host edge between selected originals. Exact lifting produced two induced, mutually anticomplete paths of 14 edges each. The straight rails select both endpoints of all four unused matching edges and fail. The normal-form argument, independently checked on this 42-vertex host, supplies H3-freeness.
claims.search_method: Constructed the exact host, lifted both straight and switched routes, checked simplicity, chords, cross-path edges, matching use, and H3 connector feasibility.

claims.claim: For arbitrary graphs, hence also for H3-free graphs, k-Induced Disjoint Paths is fixed-parameter tractable in k+b, where b is the number of vertices of degree at least three. There is an exact equivalent compression with at most b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices.
claims.evidence: With B={v:deg(v)≥3}, every component of G−B has maximum degree two and at most two attachment edges. A terminal-free component can only be used as a corridor between two distinct B vertices, and one fresh two-edge representative per unordered pair suffices. In a terminal-bearing path component with t terminals, retaining terminals and attachment occurrences leaves at most t+1≤2t gaps; a cycle has t gaps. Keeping one-edge gaps and replacing every longer gap by a two-edge path preserves exactly whether two selected marks are adjacent. Degree-two nonterminals force complete traversal, so contraction and expansion preserve paths, inducedness, disjointness, and cross-path adjacency. There are at most b+2k retained branch/terminal vertices, binom(b,2) generic representatives, and 4k gap representatives, giving the claimed bound. Exhaustive solution enumeration on that bounded graph is an FPT algorithm.
claims.witness: The explicit inverse maps contract every completely traversed degree-two gap/corridor to its representative and expand each selected representative back to its original segment. Exact testing found no discrepancy or size violation in all 67,722 labeled one- and two-pair instances through six vertices.
claims.search_method: Independent component-by-component kernel proof, followed by exhaustive comparison of original and compressed linkage truth values on every labeled graph through order six for fixed one- and two-pair terminal families.

claims.claim: A globally shortest path for one terminal pair cannot be fixed greedily, even on a seven-vertex H3-free graph.
claims.evidence: A seven-vertex graph cannot contain the eight-vertex H3 as a subgraph. Exact simple-path enumeration finds s1-x-t1 as the unique shortest s1-t1 path. Every s2-t2 path contains s2, and the host edge xs2 prevents that shortest path from belonging to an induced linkage. The longer induced path s1-y-z-t1 is vertex-disjoint and anticomplete to the edge s2-t2, so a linkage nevertheless exists.
claims.witness: Vertices s1,t1,x,s2,t2,y,z with edges s1x,xt1,xs2,s2t2,s1y,yz,zt1; the unique linkage found is (s1-y-z-t1, s2-t2).
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of all simple paths for both pairs, followed by inducedness, vertex-disjointness, and cross-edge tests.

target_evidence: The exact source target asks for a complexity classification for every fixed k on H3-subgraph-free graphs. The draft proves the k=1 case and several valid structural, obstruction, and parameterized results, but proves neither polynomial-time solvability nor NP-hardness for any fixed k≥2. It explicitly states this limitation and claims only PARTIAL resolution. The surviving results are material progress but do not complete the requested classification.
